answers.question: After a cancel call gets no answer, the agent looks the order up and, if it is still placed or processing, sends the cancel once more. Nothing says what happens when that second cancel call also gets no answer. The shortest path where it matters: the customer says yes; the cancel call gets no answer; the lookup shows the order still processing; the second cancel call gets no answer. What ends it? Claims put to the owner: C-27.
answers.recommended: The agent sends no third cancel call, says it is not known whether the order was cancelled, issues no refund, and creates a follow-up task for staff with the reason cancellation unknown.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation.

answers.question: What should the agent do when its first lookup of the customer's orders gets no answer, before anything is proposed? Under the recommendation, the shortest path is: the customer asks to cancel an order; the lookup gets no answer; the agent tells the customer it cannot look up the orders now, and nothing changes. Claims put to the owner: C-44.
answers.recommended: The agent tells the customer it cannot look up the orders now and changes nothing.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
